☰ Prerequisites & General Checks
WARNING: Make sure the landing gear downlock pins are installed before this task (TASK 32-00-01-480-801). Without them the gear can retract and cause injury / equipment damage.
WARNING: Do not push on the tire with tools or other objects. A damaged tire can explode and cause injury / equipment damage.
Tire servicing first. Service the tire per TASK 12-15-51-610-802 before inspecting (correct inflation affects the read).
Bias vs radial. Bias-ply tires must not be used on the same axle as radial-ply tires (General A.1).
General scan (3a–b). Examine for air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn areas, cuts and flat spots, and for contaminants (oils, fuels, hydraulic fluids, cleaning agents, greases).
Groove-depth method (3d). Measure each groove at three equally-spaced points and average. Any groove averaging ≤ 1/32 in (0.79 mm) = fully worn.
Location zones. 713 nose gear · 734 left main · 744 right main.
⚠ Gray-Area Judgment Calls
Zone — tread vs shoulder vs sidewall. Decides which cut rule applies. Shoulder cuts that expose fabric are "remove immediately" (Sht 3), but where the shoulder still carries tread, the tread-cut rules apply (into plies = not serviceable). Set the cut zone in the calculator.
Reinforcement vs carcass/belt fabric. Cut protector / tread reinforcement showing = deferrable; carcass/belt ply (fabric / body cord) showing = NOT serviceable. The reinforcement can be metal or Kevlar — a visual call.
Chevron single-cut limits. This task does NOT quantify them. You must reference the Fig 602 single-cut limits / standard practices — the tool cannot compute that threshold.
Worn area mimicking a groove bottom. Per Sht 8, worn tread below the original groove can look like a groove bottom. Measure depth at 3 points and average.
"Tire balance affected." Flat-spot / ice-burn serviceability can hinge on whether balance is affected — an inspector judgment.
Open vs closed tread splice. A closed splice (thin line crossing the ribs) is acceptable; an open splice is not serviceable.
